exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 Too Many Selfies
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Mia: You've taken about twenty selfies of the same moment, Tom.
Tom: I know. I just can't post one until it looks perfect.
Mia: But you edit them so much that they don't even look like you.
Tom: That's the point. I remove every mark and make my eyes bigger.
Mia: Honestly, I think you look better in the real photos.
Tom: Do you really? I always feel my real face isn't good enough.
Mia: It is. The people who care about you like the true you, not a screen version.
Tom: Maybe you're right. I'll try posting one without any editing today.
exercises.translation_cn: Mia 说 Tom 为同一个瞬间拍了二十张自拍;Tom 说不修到完美就不肯发;Mia 觉得他修得太厉害,都不像本人了;Tom 说就是要去掉瑕疵、放大眼睛;Mia 觉得他真实照片更好看;Tom 总觉得真脸不够好;Mia 说在乎他的人喜欢真实的他;Tom 决定试着发一张不修的。

options: He wants it to look perfect first.
He has no internet at home.
He does not like the place.

questions.stem: What does Tom do to his photos?
options: He prints them for his wall.
He removes marks and enlarges his eyes.

questions.stem: What does Mia think of his real photos?
How does Tom feel about his real face?
options: He is very proud of it.
He feels it is not good enough.
He wants to show it to everyone.

questions.stem: What does Tom decide to do at the end?
options: Post a photo without editing it.

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 Be Kind to Yourself
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Here is a simple thought for anyone who feels unhappy with their looks.
The way you speak to yourself matters more than any mirror.
If you call yourself ugly every day, you will start to believe it.
Try to notice one thing you like about yourself instead.
A kinder voice inside your head can change the whole day.
exercises.translation_cn: 给对外貌不满的人一个简单的想法:你对自己说话的方式比任何镜子都重要;如果天天骂自己丑,就会真的相信;不如试着找出一件自己喜欢的地方;脑海里更友善的声音能改变一整天。

questions.stem: Who is this advice for?
options: Anyone unhappy with how they look.

questions.stem: What does the speaker say matters most?
options: The way you talk to yourself.

questions.stem: What happens if you call yourself ugly every day?
options: You will start to believe it.
You will look in the mirror less.

questions.stem: What does the speaker suggest doing instead?
options: Noticing one thing you like about yourself.

questions.stem: What can a kinder inner voice do?

exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 A New Haircut
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Leo: Wow, Anna, you've cut your hair really short. It looks great.
Anna: Thanks. I was nervous, but I wanted to try a new style.
Leo: What made you decide to change it?
Anna: I'd kept the same long hair for years just because everyone expected it.
Leo: So this is more about being yourself than about fashion?
Anna: Exactly. The new cut feels like the real me, not a copy of others.
Leo: I think confidence is what really suits you, more than any hairstyle.
Anna: That's kind of you. I do feel more confident already.
exercises.translation_cn: Leo 夸 Anna 剪了短发好看;Anna 说本来很紧张,但想试试新风格;为什么要改变?多年留长发只因大家都期待如此;Leo 问这更多是做自己而非追时尚?Anna 说没错,新发型才像真正的自己;Leo 说真正适合她的是自信;Anna 说她确实已经更自信了。

questions.stem: What has Anna done to her hair?

options: She had no time for haircuts.

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 First Impressions
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: When we meet someone new, we often judge them in just a few seconds.
A neat appearance can leave a warm first impression.
But that first impression is only the cover of a very long book.
Kindness, honesty and humour are what make people truly attractive.
So look after how you appear, but never stop there.
exercises.translation_cn: 我们遇到新朋友时,常常几秒钟就下判断;整洁的外表能留下温暖的第一印象;但第一印象只是一本厚书的封面;善良、诚实和幽默才让人真正有魅力;所以要注意外表,但别止步于此。

options: The cover of a long book.

questions.stem: What truly makes people attractive, according to the passage?

options: Care about your looks, but do not stop there.

exercises.title: U1 听力·对话 Exercise for Health
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: Sam: You go running twice a week now. Are you trying to lose weight?
Grace: Not really. I used to exercise only to become thin, but not anymore.
Sam: So why do you keep doing it?
Grace: Now I run because it makes me feel strong and healthy.
Sam: That sounds much better than chasing a number on the scales.
Grace: It is. I once took weight-loss pills, and they only made me ill.
Sam: I'm glad you stopped. Health really should come first.
Grace: Exactly. I'd rather be fit and happy than thin and miserable.
exercises.translation_cn: Sam 问 Grace 现在一周跑两次是想减肥吗?Grace 说不是,以前只为变瘦,现在不了;那为什么坚持?因为跑步让她感到强壮健康;Sam 说这比盯着体重数字好多了;Grace 说曾吃减肥药,结果只让自己生病;Sam 庆幸她停了,健康该放第一;Grace 说宁愿健康快乐,也不要瘦却痛苦。

questions.stem: Why does Grace run now?
Why did Grace exercise in the past?

options: Running for health is much better.

questions.stem: What happened when Grace took weight-loss pills?

options: Fit and happy rather than thin and miserable.

exercises.title: U1 听力·短文 Beauty Within a Book
exercises.speaker: uk_female
transcript: In one famous old novel, a man is born with a frightening face.
People treat him cruelly and never look for the heart inside.
Yet when a young woman shows him a small act of kindness, everything changes.
He risks his own life to protect her from danger.
The story reminds us that real worth is found within, not on the surface.
exercises.translation_cn: 在一部著名的老小说里,一个男人生来面孔可怕;人们残忍地对待他,从不去发现他内心;然而当一位年轻女子向他展现一点善意,一切都改变了;他冒着生命危险保护她免遭危险;故事提醒我们:真正的价值在内心,而非表面。
